Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up and the usage file. Quick summary and a proposal so your procurement team can review: 

1) Short-term burst (what we can offer)
- Lead time: we can enable a controlled burst within 24–48 hours for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted accounts typically take 48–72 hours to provision depending on regional capacity.
- Max uplift: for a predictable short window we can support up to 2x baseline in most regions; you requested ~1.5x which is straightforward.

2) Overrun / true-up mechanics (two options)
- Standard overrun: excess tokens billed at published on-demand rates for the month; a monthly true-up invoice covers any usage above committed units.
- Blended/bridge option (what I recommend for predictability): we offer a temporary blended rate for bursts — a discounted uplift price that applies to incremental tokens during the burst window, then we do a single true-up invoice at the end of the month that reconciles committed vs actual. For example: if your standard incremental rate is $0.012/token on-demand, we can offer a blended burst rate of $0.009/token for the 3–4 week window.

3) Short-term credit / bridge discount
- For a 4-week burst we can add a one-time bridge credit of $5,000 applied to the true-up invoice if you commit to a follow-on 3-month usage evaluation (this helps us prioritize capacity and gives you budget certainty). Alternatively, we can trade a 7.5% discount on incremental usage in exchange for a 60-day commitment to target throughput.

Next steps (recommended):
- I can push a short-term addendum (one page) that captures burst start/end dates, uplift cap, blended rate, and the bridge credit option.
- If that works, I’ll create the HubSpot deal record + DocuSign link and loop finance for PO/invoice flow.

I attached a draft rate-sheet for internal procurement review: proposed-bridge-rate-sheet.pdf. Laura — would love a quick read to confirm we can approve the $5k credit for Orbit AI under our standard enterprise playbook.
